active_work_package.title: Platform repository skeleton from the P0.2 design
active_work_package.objective: Create the place every later package lands, shaped so the modular monolith boundaries are tested rather than intended: the workspace and layout, the module registry, the seven dependency rules generated from it, the migration lint, the boundary test suite that proves both fire, the charter, these records and their schemas, and the CI skeleton. It implements no epic and creates no domain table.

stop_reason: Independent peer review has now returned REVISION_REQUIRED four times. Rounds one to three are recorded in DEC-006 to DEC-021. Round four reviewed the work that closed round three's declared-open findings, and its result is the reason this entry is worth reading: the individual fixes were sound and the WHOLE was not. Two findings could only be seen from the whole. First, a CRITICAL total bypass - PostgreSQL documents SET SCHEMA 'value' as an alias for SET search_path TO value, and three words of legal SQL let a migration set the session schema to audit and then create tables, defaults and index expressions that all bound into another module's schema, with the lint reporting PASS and exit 0. Second, one task's extractors had silently narrowed an earlier task's deny-by-default, because an incidental own-schema target satisfied the understood flag, so COMMENT ON FUNCTION, GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION and SECURITY LABEL all passed again after being refused. Neither was visible to any per-task review; both were found by reading the six changes together. Round four also found the FOURTH instance of this repository's recurring defect - six refusals in the record validator deletable with the whole suite green - and, in the fix wave itself, a test seam that neutered the coverage gate and all four of its own witnesses through one exported environment variable. Every finding is closed and witnessed. WP-001 stays at ENGINEERING_READY. Every reviewer so far has been an agent; none is the independent human verifier the P0.2 design names, and no re-review of this head has happened. NS-001 remains primary and remains half done: branch protection is applied and negative control 6 is observed, but the repository-administrator seat is unfilled, and badf/agents.yaml now records held_by for every seat as null and refuses any other value, so filling one is a reviewed change to the validator under a Work Package - which is what a human decision should cost.
known_divergence: The boundary rules here are the PROPOSAL of a design at IN_REVIEW that depends on five ADRs, all DRAFT_REQUIRED. If ADR-001 narrows or widens the seven rules, the registry and the generator change with it and the suite is re-run. FOUR review rounds have now found the same defect, and it has never once been a wrong rule: the suite was green while a rule did nothing. Four dependency rules loosenable with no fixture going red; two controls surviving their own rule being disabled; three of four audit verbs and two of four domain words named in AGENTS.md section 5 and witnessed by nothing; then six refusals in the record validator, and both arms of rules 5 and 5b on the apps side. The response is no longer a list of fixes. It is scripts/coverage-gate.mjs, which fails the build when a protection this repository names has no fixture asserting its message and derives that list from the code so it cannot drift; DEC-022, which makes the unit of coverage the statement type rather than the message; and 98 mutations, up from 24 when this pattern was first recorded. TWO THINGS ARE WORTH STATING PLAINLY BECAUSE THEY ARE UNCOMFORTABLE. First, round four found that a later change had silently narrowed an earlier change's default, and no per-task review could have seen it - only reading the six changes together did. A review that reads each change in isolation cannot find that class at all. Second, the fix wave for round four introduced the defect class INTO THE INSTRUMENT BUILT TO DETECT IT: a test seam let one exported environment variable neuter the coverage gate and all four of its witnesses simultaneously. It was caught by the re-review, and the seam is now a command-line argument that nothing can inherit. Both are recorded here rather than in a commit message because they are the strongest available evidence for why an independent verifier, reading the whole, is not a formality this repository can skip. The residual gap named in the round-three records is unchanged and remains the most important line: a forgery that edits badf/authority.yaml, badf/current-state.json and the checkpoint CONSISTENTLY still passes every check here, because nothing binds a record to a human identity. No validator closes that. The mechanism that addresses it is the approval requirement now enforced on main.
